sourceEvidence.label: SEIS local secret-boundary control audit at db817330
sourceEvidence.driftScope: Derived documentation and parallel implementation work were added after the evidence snapshot; executable controls must be refreshed before implementation.

assessment.summary: The audit supports one cross-cutting opportunity to replace convention-based secret safeguards with deterministic local controls; no proposal is implemented by this analysis.

nonNegotiables: Never print, store, or reproduce a secret value.
Do not install tools or elevate privileges from the local scan wrapper.
Do not rotate credentials, broaden allowlists, rewrite history, or close issue 129 without human approval.
Keep public demo and repository validation usable without credentials.
Use explicit least-privilege permissions and integrity-verifiable tool acquisition.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
A formal Codex Security scan was not run.
The open historical exception remains unresolved until the accountable human records a disposition.

opportunities.title: Make local secret-boundary enforcement deterministic
opportunities.summary: Consolidate placeholder, ignore, scanner, workflow, policy, and incident invariants into locally owned executable gates.
opportunities.diagnosis: Important secret-handling invariants are distributed across conventions and documents, while the local scanner can mutate the workstation and the remote pass remains conditional on an unresolved historical exception.

evidence.claim: Broad ignore rules can hide new workflow, security-script, and security-document controls from ordinary untracked-file inspection.
A public-safe environment template exists, but no deterministic check owns placeholder-only secret fields.
The scanner configuration includes a path-level exception for the historical generated aggregation tracked by open issue 129.
The Guardian workflow scans with redaction but uses implicit permissions and a versioned scanner download without recorded digest verification.
The local wrapper can install tools or elevate privileges, omits a redaction flag in its scan invocation, and suggests destructive history cleanup without an approval workflow.
Repository policies establish strong intent but did not provide one complete storage lifecycle, incident runbook, and executable ownership boundary at the evidence revision.
The configured scan passed for the evidence revision while the owner decision for excluded historical content remained open.
Control ownership is convention-based enough that a future contributor can preserve one layer while weakening or bypassing another.

desiredInvariants: Every secret-named field in a public environment template is deterministically classified as a public-safe placeholder without printing its value.
Every local secret scan is redacted, non-installing, non-privileged, and side-effect free apart from its documented exit status.
Every remote secret scan runs with explicit least-privilege permissions and an integrity-verifiable scanner distribution.
Every configured exception has a narrow rationale, owner, evidence link, review state, and explicit effect on security claims.
Every suspected credential exposure enters one path-only incident process that requires owner authority for revocation, rotation, or history recovery.
A passing check reports its revision, scope, exceptions, and skipped surfaces rather than implying universal absence of secrets.

options.title: Deterministic repository-local controls
options.summary: Own storage, placeholder, ignore, scanner, workflow, incident, and evidence invariants in focused local validation and CI gates.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Focused ignore rules and regression checks make control paths visible.
A value-redacting template validator owns the placeholder invariant.
The scanner wrapper and workflow require focused source changes even after the structural local boundary is chosen.
Canonical policy and incident links give the executable checks one documented owner.
The option makes conditional evidence explicit but cannot decide or remediate the historical exception without its owner.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deterministic checks close the observed local bypass and redaction gaps, while the historical exception remains owner-gated.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run negative fixtures for unsafe placeholders, ignored control paths, non-redacted invocation, implicit permissions, and misleading summary states.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local metadata checks add bounded repository validation work; full-history Gitleaks already exists in CI.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record validator wall time and Guardian job duration before and after the change; fail review if local validation becomes materially disruptive.

tradeoffs.assessment: The validator needs only small path and configuration records and introduces no retained service state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the validator against the repository and confirm it does not construct or serialize file contents beyond bounded template lines.

tradeoffs.assessment: A missing local tool fails safely instead of initiating an unreviewed installation, and CI status semantics become explicit.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise missing-tool, cancelled-job, scanner-failure, and invalid-template cases and verify deterministic nonzero exits.

tradeoffs.assessment: One command and one incident handoff reduce ambiguity without adding a service, though maintainers must review scanner pins and exceptions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Perform a credential-free tabletop and confirm a contributor can locate the policy, run the check, and interpret every status.

tradeoffs.assessment: The approach preserves repository layout and current CI while replacing unsafe behavior in focused files.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Land work packages independently, run compatibility checks after each, and verify rollback by reverting one package at a time.

residualRisks: The historical exception remains unresolved until the accountable human records a disposition.
Repository-local controls can diverge across future canonical repositories.
No scanner proves absence outside its configured scope or retained downstream copies.

workPackages: Add deterministic secret-boundary validation and negative fixtures.
Make the local scanner redacted, non-installing, and incident-aware.
Apply explicit workflow permissions and integrity-verifiable scanner acquisition.
Replace broad control-path ignore rules with focused secret and local-artifact rules.
Record remote evidence and retain issue 129 as an owner decision gate.
acceptanceCriteria: Unsafe template, ignore, scanner, workflow, and summary fixtures fail without printing values.
Local validation performs no installation, elevation, provider call, or external write.
Guardian CI passes at the implementation revision with redaction and explicit permissions.
Issue 129 remains open or has an owner-approved disposition with redacted evidence.
migrationNotes: Preserve current redacted CI scanning while local controls are introduced.
Do not change the historical allowlist in the implementation slice without a separate owner decision.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert each focused validator, wrapper, workflow, ignore, and documentation package independently while retaining redaction and the incident boundary.

options.title: Centralized ecosystem security enforcement
options.summary: Move policy, scanner acquisition, validation, exception ownership, and evidence formatting into a versioned shared security control package or isolated runner.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Central ownership reduces repository-local drift, but the current unsafe wrapper and workflow still need tactical correction during migration.
A central exception register improves governance but cannot make the historical owner decision.

tradeoffs.assessment: Central policy and scanner ownership reduce cross-repository drift but introduce a new highly trusted package or runner.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model package publication, runner authority, update channels, rollback, and consumer pinning before adoption.

tradeoffs.assessment: A reusable action or remote runner may add setup, download, or invocation overhead not present in local metadata checks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype one consumer and compare cold and warm job duration against the local option.

tradeoffs.assessment: A packaged action is likely bounded, while a persistent service would add process and queue state; no design has been selected.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Choose the delivery model first, then measure peak runner memory and retained evidence size.

tradeoffs.assessment: Consumers gain consistent behavior but depend on a shared release or runner whose outage or bad update can block every repository.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test pinned-version operation, unavailable-central-control behavior, rollback, and last-known-good recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: The ecosystem must own package releases, compatibility, exception governance, observability, and incident response for a new trusted component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define an owner, release SLO, supported consumer matrix, signing or digest policy, and emergency rollback before implementation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing repository-local controls must remain active until every consumer pins and validates the shared contract.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Migrate one repository at a time with parity fixtures and preserve dual enforcement until results match.

residualRisks: Compromise or drift in the central control can affect every consumer.
Repository-specific exceptions may be flattened into unsafe generic policy.
Issue 129 still requires an accountable human decision.

affectedComponents: future ecosystem security package or isolated runner
workPackages: Define canonical ownership and a versioned policy contract.
Threat-model the distribution and execution boundary.
Prototype one read-only consumer with pinned integrity.
Validate parity before migrating additional repositories.
acceptanceCriteria: A consumer can pin, validate, and roll back the central control without ambient write authority.
Repository-specific exceptions remain explicit and reviewable.
An unavailable central control fails closed with a documented recovery path.
migrationNotes: Do not remove local controls until parity and rollback evidence exist.
Do not centralize private credential material; centralize policy and enforcement only.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Pin consumers to the last-known-good version or restore repository-local enforcement while the central control is disabled.

opportunities.recommendation: Select deterministic repository-local controls now because they address observed gaps without adding a new trusted service; revisit central enforcement when multiple canonical repositories require the same stable contract.

selectionBasis: The user requested autonomous development under least privilege, and the local option is the smallest reversible design that directly addresses the inspected controls.

limitations: Gitleaks was unavailable locally, so the local repository and history scan was not executed.
The previous remote Guardian run applies to source evidence revision db817330, not the implementation working tree.
Issue 129 remains open and the configured historical exception remains unresolved.

openQuestions: Which integrity-verifiable Gitleaks distribution mechanism should become canonical?
What owner-approved disposition will close or narrow the historical exception tracked by issue 129?
At what number of canonical consumer repositories should central enforcement be reconsidered?
